questions: Have your eyes recently started to look more prominent or bulge forward?
Have both eyes changed in appearance at about the same time?
Have you noticed blurred or reduced vision?
Do you have eye pain, especially when moving your eyes?
Have your eyes become unusually dry, gritty, watery, or sensitive to light?
Have you had redness or swelling of the eyelids?
Have you been unable to close either eye completely during sleep?
Have you had a recent eye injury or eye surgery?
Have you ever been diagnosed with thyroid disease?
Have you recently had weight loss, heat intolerance, sweating, tremor, or a fast heartbeat?
Have you noticed a neck swelling or thyroid lump?
Do you smoke or use nicotine products?
Have you started any new medicines or supplements recently?
Have you had a severe headache, drooping eyelid, unequal pupils, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking?

results: 1. Monocular and binocular visual-acuity testing
not performed / not available
2. Pupillary examination, including anisocoria assessment in bright and dim light
pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
3. Ocular-alignment examination with the cover–uncover and alternate-cover tests at distance and near
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
4. Prism measurement of the ocular deviation in primary position and in the nine diagnostic positions of gaze
not performed / not available
5. Duction and version testing, including saccades and smooth pursuit
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
6. Assessment for ocular motility restriction and forced-duction testing if restriction is suspected
forced duction test: not performed
7. Examination for ptosis, fatigability, and Cogan lid-twitch sign
ptosis / lid position: partial ptosis
8. Measurement of ocular torsion with double Maddox rods
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
9. Complete cranial-nerve and neurologic examination
cranial nerve examination: partial right oculomotor palsy with right adduction failure, mild vertical gaze limitation, mildly impaired convergence, and partial ptosis; pupils equally reactive
10. Thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine levels
TSH / free T4: normal
11. Acetylcholine-receptor antibody and MuSK-antibody testing
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
12. MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast, including the cavernous sinuses and brainstem
MRI brain with gadolinium: small dorsal paramedian midbrain infarct
MRI sella and orbits: normal pituitary and orbits
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Pupil-sparing partial right oculomotor (CN III) palsy caused by a small dorsal paramedian midbrain ischemic infarction (fascicular midbrain stroke)

ALTERNATIVE: Ocular myasthenia gravis

ALTERNATIVE: Small midbrain demyelinating lesion

ALTERNATIVE: Compressive right oculomotor nerve lesion not detected on current imaging
